items.stem: A peacock spreads its colorful tail feathers when a female is nearby. What type of behavior is this?

options.text: A nest-building behavior
A mating display
A way to find food
A method of camouflage

items.explanation: Spreading colorful feathers to be noticed and chosen by a mate is a mating display.

items.stem: Why do hummingbird-pollinated flowers often have bright red colors?

options.text: Bright color attracts pollinators that carry pollen between flowers
Bright color scares away all insects
Color makes the flower taste better
Color blocks sunlight from reaching the seeds

items.explanation: Birds see red well, so a bright red flower attracts the pollinator that carries its pollen, which helps seeds form.

items.stem: Why do maple seeds have thin, wing-like structures that make them spin as they fall?

options.text: To attract bees to the seed
To make the tree grow taller
To help the seeds travel far from the parent tree on the wind
To store extra water for the seed

items.explanation: The spinning wing helps the seed glide on the wind. This is seed dispersal, spreading seeds away from the parent so more can grow.

items.stem: How does parental care increase reproductive success?

options.text: It makes the parents grow much larger
It changes the weather around the nest
It removes the need to find a mate
It raises the chance that offspring survive to reproduce

items.explanation: Protecting and feeding young means more of them survive long enough to grow up and reproduce.

items.stem: Burrs have tiny hooks that stick to the fur of passing animals. What does this structure help the plant do?

options.text: Attract pollinators with a sweet scent
Spread its seeds to new places
Make food from sunlight
Stay warm during the winter

items.explanation: Hooks let the seed hitch a ride on an animal's fur, dispersing it far from the parent plant.

items.stem: Emperor penguins take turns balancing their egg on their feet to keep it warm through the freezing winter. This is an example of:

options.text: Parental care
A mating display
Seed dispersal
Pollination

items.explanation: Protecting an egg so the chick survives is parental care, a behavior that raises reproductive success.

items.stem: A male cardinal sings loudly from the edge of an area and chases off other males. What behavior is this?

options.text: Parental care
Pollination
Territorial behavior
Camouflage

items.explanation: Defending an area that holds food and nesting space is territorial behavior. It protects the resources needed to raise young.

items.stem: Which statement best uses evidence to explain why a flower produces sweet nectar?

options.text: Nectar has no role in reproduction
Nectar attracts pollinators, which carry pollen and increase the chance that seeds form
Nectar makes the flower heavier so it falls to the ground
Nectar cools the plant on hot days

items.explanation: Nectar rewards pollinators for visiting. As they feed, they move pollen between flowers, which raises the chance of pollination and seeds.

items.stem: A peacock's large tail takes energy to grow and makes the bird easier for predators to see. Why has this trait continued over many generations?

options.text: The tail helps the peacock fly faster
The tail keeps the bird warm
The tail has no effect on survival or reproduction
Peahens choose mates with impressive tails, so those males reproduce more

items.explanation: A costly trait can persist if it raises reproductive success. Peahens favor large, bright tails, so those males leave more offspring and the trait is passed on.

items.stem: Which pair correctly matches a strategy used by animals with one used by plants?

options.text: Courtship displays in animals; colorful flowers in plants
Photosynthesis in animals; nest building in plants
Pollination in animals; territorial songs in plants
Seed dispersal in animals; mating dances in plants

items.explanation: Animals use behaviors like courtship displays, and plants use structures like colorful flowers. Both raise the chance of successful reproduction.
